content:
Build an Android app for nurses at a small clinic to track antenatal care
(ANC) visits.

1. **Register screen:** a list of currently pregnant patients showing name,
   age, estimated due date, and current weeks of pregnancy, sorted by due
   date (soonest first).
2. Tapping a patient opens a **patient detail screen** showing her past ANC
   visits: date, weight, blood pressure, and hemoglobin if recorded.
3. From the detail screen the nurse can **record a new ANC visit** by
   filling a form with: visit date, gestational age in weeks, weight (kg),
   systolic and diastolic blood pressure (mmHg), any danger signs (none /
   vaginal bleeding / severe headache / blurred vision / fever, multiple
   allowed), and free-text notes.
4. Saving the form persists the visit; it appears in the patient's visit
   list and survives app restart.

The clinic already has these three patients on file, each with one prior
visit:

| Name | Date of birth | Est. due date | Last visit | Weight | BP | Hb |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Emily Carter | 1996-04-12 | 2026-12-05 | 2026-08-10 | 68.5 kg | 118/76 | 11.8 g/dL |
| Sarah Mitchell | 1990-11-02 | 2027-01-20 | 2026-08-12 | 61.2 kg | 110/70 | 12.4 g/dL |
| Grace Thompson | 2001-07-30 | 2026-10-15 | 2026-08-05 | 72.0 kg | 128/84 | 10.2 g/dL |

A FHIR R4 server (HAPI) is running at `http://10.0.2.2:8080/fhir` (Android
emulator's address for the host machine; no auth). It already contains the
three patients as `Patient` resources with linked `Encounter` and
`Observation` resources (due date, weight, blood pressure, hemoglobin), and
a `Questionnaire` with id `anc-contact` for the ANC visit form. The project
has kotlin-fhir R4 types (`dev.ohs.fhir:fhir-model`), FHIR Engine
(`dev.ohs.fhir:fhir-engine`), and the Data Capture library
(`dev.ohs.fhir:fhir-data-capture`) on the classpath. Use the server as the
source of truth and the Questionnaire for the visit form.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

package dev.ohs.fhir.engine.sync

import dev.ohs.fhir.engine.FhirEngine
import dev.ohs.fhir.engine.FhirEngineProvider
import dev.ohs.fhir.engine.sync.download.DownloaderImpl
import dev.ohs.fhir.engine.sync.upload.UploadStrategy
import dev.ohs.fhir.engine.sync.upload.Uploader
import dev.ohs.fhir.engine.sync.upload.patch.PatchGeneratorFactory
import dev.ohs.fhir.engine.sync.upload.request.UploadRequestGeneratorFactory
import kotlinx.coroutines.cancel
import kotlinx.coroutines.coroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch

/**
 */
interface FhirSyncTask {
  fun getFhirEngine(): FhirEngine

  fun getDownloadWorkManager(): DownloadWorkManager

  fun getConflictResolver(): ConflictResolver

  fun getUploadStrategy(): UploadStrategy
}

/**
 *
 *
 */
suspend fun FhirSyncTask.runSync(
  taskName: String?,
  onProgress: suspend (SyncJobStatus) -> Unit,
): SyncJobStatus {
  val fhirDataStore = FhirEngineProvider.getFhirDataStore()
  val dataSource =
    FhirEngineProvider.getDataSource()
      ?: throw IllegalStateException(
        "FhirEngineConfiguration.ServerConfiguration is not set. Call FhirEngineProvider.init to initialize with appropriate configuration.",
      )

  val uploadStrategy = getUploadStrategy()
  val synchronizer =
    FhirSynchronizer(
      getFhirEngine(),
      UploadConfiguration(
        uploader =
          Uploader(
            dataSource = dataSource,
            patchGenerator = PatchGeneratorFactory.byMode(uploadStrategy.patchGeneratorMode),
            requestGenerator =
              UploadRequestGeneratorFactory.byMode(uploadStrategy.requestGeneratorMode),
          ),
        uploadStrategy = uploadStrategy,
      ),
      DownloadConfiguration(
        DownloaderImpl(dataSource, getDownloadWorkManager()),
        getConflictResolver(),
      ),
      fhirDataStore,
    )

  return coroutineScope {
    launch(syncDispatcher) {
      synchronizer.syncState.collect { syncJobStatus ->
        when (syncJobStatus) {
          is SyncJobStatus.Succeeded,
          is SyncJobStatus.Failed, -> {
            if (taskName != null) {
              fhirDataStore.writeTerminalSyncJobStatus(taskName, syncJobStatus)
            }
            cancel()
          }
          else -> onProgress(syncJobStatus)
        }
      }
    }

    synchronizer.synchronize()
  }
}

package dev.ohs.fhir.datacapture

import android.content.Context

actual object DataCapture {

  private lateinit var configuration: DataCaptureConfig

  fun initialize(context: Context) {
    if (!::configuration.isInitialized) {
      configuration =
        if (context.applicationContext is DataCaptureConfig.Provider) {
          (context.applicationContext as DataCaptureConfig.Provider).getDataCaptureConfig()
        } else {
          DataCaptureConfig()
        }
    }
    return
  }

  actual fun getConfiguration(): DataCaptureConfig {
    if (this::configuration.isInitialized) {
      return configuration
    } else {
      throw Exception(
        "DataCapture not initialized. Initialize the library with DataCapture.initialize(context) "
      )
    }
  }
}

@OptIn(ExperimentalTime::class)
internal class QuestionnaireViewModel(state: Map<String, Any>) : ViewModel() {
  private val jsonR4 = Json {
    explicitNulls = false
    encodeDefaults = false
  }
  private val xFhirQueryResolver: XFhirQueryResolver? by lazy {
    DataCapture.getConfiguration().xFhirQueryResolver
  }
  private val externalValueSetResolver: ExternalAnswerValueSetResolver? by lazy {
    DataCapture.getConfiguration().valueSetResolverExternal
  }

  /** The current questionnaire as questions are being answered. */
  internal val questionnaire: Questionnaire

  init {
    questionnaire =
      when {
        state.contains(EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_JSON_URI) -> {
          if (state.contains(EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_JSON_STRING)) {
            Logger.w(
              "Both EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_JSON_URI & EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_JSON_STRING are provided. " +
                "EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_JSON_URI takes precedence."
            )
          }
          val uriPath: String = state[EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_JSON_URI] as String
          jsonR4.decodeFromString(readFileContent(uriPath)) as Questionnaire
        }

        state.contains(EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_JSON_STRING) -> {
          val questionnaireJson: String = state[EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_JSON_STRING] as String
          jsonR4.decodeFromString(questionnaireJson) as Questionnaire
        }

        else ->
          error(
            "Neither EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_JSON_URI nor EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_JSON_STRING is supplied."
          )
      }
  }

  /** The current questionnaire response as questions are being answered. */
  private val questionnaireResponse: MutableStateFlow<QuestionnaireResponse> =
    MutableStateFlow(QuestionnaireResponse.Builder(Enumeration()).build())

  init {
    val questionnaireResponseDraft: QuestionnaireResponse

    when {
      state.contains(EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_RESPONSE_JSON_URI) -> {
        if (state.contains(EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_RESPONSE_JSON_STRING)) {
          Logger.w(
            "Both EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_RESPONSE_JSON_URI & EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_RESPONSE_JSON_STRING are provided. " +
              "EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_RESPONSE_JSON_URI takes precedence."
          )
        }

        questionnaireResponseDraft =
          jsonR4.decodeFromString(
            readFileContent(state[EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_RESPONSE_JSON_URI]!! as String)
          ) as QuestionnaireResponse

        addMissingResponseItems(questionnaire.item, questionnaireResponseDraft.item.toMutableList())
        checkQuestionnaireResponse(questionnaire, questionnaireResponseDraft)
      }

      state.contains(EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_RESPONSE_JSON_STRING) -> {
        val questionnaireResponseJson: String =
          state[EXTRA_QUESTIONNAIRE_RESPONSE_JSON_STRING] as String

package com.example.ancapp.data

import com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum.decimal.BigDecimal
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.Code
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.CodeableConcept
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.Coding

import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.HumanName

import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.Quantity
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.Reference
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.Uri
import java.time.LocalDate
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.Decimal as FhirDecimal
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.String as FhirString

/* ---------- constructing primitives ---------- */

fun str(value: String): FhirString = FhirString(value = value)

fun uri(value: String): Uri = Uri(value = value)

fun code(value: String): Code = Code(value = value)

fun decimal(value: String): FhirDecimal = FhirDecimal(value = BigDecimal.parseString(value))

fun reference(value: String): Reference = Reference(reference = str(value))

fun coding(system: String, codeValue: String, display: String? = null): Coding =
  Coding(system = uri(system), code = code(codeValue), display = display?.let { str(it) })

fun codeableConcept(coding: Coding, text: String? = null): CodeableConcept =
  CodeableConcept(coding = listOf(coding), text = text?.let { str(it) })

fun quantity(value: String, unit: String, ucumCode: String): Quantity =
  Quantity(value = decimal(value), unit = str(unit), system = uri(Codes.UCUM), code = code(ucumCode))

/* ---------- reading values ---------- */

/**
 * FHIR dates may be partial (year, year-month or full date). Only full dates are useful here, so
 * anything shorter is treated as absent.
 */
private fun parseFullDate(text: String?): LocalDate? =
  text?.takeIf { it.length >= 10 }?.let { runCatching { LocalDate.parse(it.substring(0, 10)) }.getOrNull() }

fun FhirDate?.toLocalDate(): LocalDate? = parseFullDate(this?.toString())

fun FhirDateTime?.toLocalDate(): LocalDate? = parseFullDate(this?.toString())

fun toFhirDate(date: LocalDate): FhirDate = FhirDate.Date(kotlinx.datetime.LocalDate.parse(date.toString()))

fun toFhirDateTime(date: LocalDate): FhirDateTime =
  FhirDateTime.Date(kotlinx.datetime.LocalDate.parse(date.toString()))

/** Renders a [HumanName] as "Given Family", falling back to `text`. */
fun HumanName.display(): String {
  val parts = (given.mapNotNull { it.value } + listOfNotNull(family?.value)).filter { it.isNotBlank() }
  return if (parts.isNotEmpty()) parts.joinToString(" ") else text?.value.orEmpty()
}

/** True if this observation carries [codeValue] from the LOINC code system. */
fun Observation.hasLoincCode(codeValue: String): Boolean =
  code.coding.any { it.system?.value == Codes.LOINC && it.code?.value == codeValue }

/** Logical id of the resource this reference points at, e.g. `Encounter/abc` -> `abc`. */
fun Reference?.targetId(): String? = this?.reference?.value?.substringAfterLast('/')

val Observation.quantityValue: Quantity?
  get() = (value as? Observation.Value.Quantity)?.value

val Observation.stringValue: String?
  get() = (value as? Observation.Value.String)?.value?.value

val Observation.dateTimeValue: FhirDateTime?
  get() = (value as? Observation.Value.DateTime)?.value?.value

val Observation.codeableConceptValue: CodeableConcept?
  get() = (value as? Observation.Value.CodeableConcept)?.value

val Observation.effectiveDate: LocalDate?
  get() =
    when (val e = effective) {
      is Observation.Effective.DateTime -> e.value.value.toLocalDate()
      is Observation.Effective.Period -> e.value.start?.value.toLocalDate()
      is Observation.Effective.Instant -> parseFullDate(e.value.value?.toString())
      else -> null
    }

fun Quantity.asDouble(): Double? = value?.value?.doubleValue(false)

/** Component of a blood-pressure panel identified by its LOINC code. */
fun Observation.component(loincCode: String): Quantity? =
  component
    .firstOrNull { c -> c.code.coding.any { it.system?.value == Codes.LOINC && it.code?.value == loincCode } }
    ?.let { (it.value as? Observation.Component.Value.Quantity)?.value }

package com.example.ancapp.data

import com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum.decimal.BigDecimal
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.Canonical
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.CodeableConcept
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.Coding
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.Encounter
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.Enumeration
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.FhirDateTime
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.Observation
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.Period
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.QuestionnaireResponse
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.Resource
import java.time.LocalDate
import java.util.UUID
import kotlinx.datetime.TimeZone
import kotlinx.datetime.toLocalDateTime
import dev.ohs.fhir.model.r4.DateTime as FhirDateTimeElement

/**
 * Turns a completed `anc-contact` [QuestionnaireResponse] into the resources that record the visit:
 * an [Encounter] for the contact itself, an [Observation] per measurement, and the response as
 * filled in by the nurse.
 */
fun extractAncContact(patientId: String, response: QuestionnaireResponse): List<Resource> {
  val answers = response.answersByLinkId()
  val visitDate = answers.date(LinkIds.VISIT_DATE) ?: LocalDate.now()
  val encounterId = "anc-enc-${UUID.randomUUID()}"
  val subject = reference("Patient/$patientId")
  val encounterRef = reference("Encounter/$encounterId")
  val effective = Observation.Effective.DateTime(FhirDateTimeElement(value = toFhirDateTime(visitDate)))

  fun observation(
    code: CodeableConcept,
    value: Observation.Value,
    category: Coding? = null,
    component: List<Observation.Component> = emptyList(),
  ) =
    Observation(
      id = "anc-obs-${UUID.randomUUID()}",
      status = Enumeration(value = Observation.ObservationStatus.Final),
      category = category?.let { listOf(codeableConcept(it)) } ?: emptyList(),
      code = code,
      subject = subject,
      encounter = encounterRef,
      effective = effective,
      value = value,
      component = component,
    )

  val resources = mutableListOf<Resource>()

  resources +=
    Encounter(
      id = encounterId,
      status = Enumeration(value = Encounter.EncounterStatus.Finished),
      `class` = coding(Codes.ACT_CODE, "AMB", "ambulatory"),
      type = listOf(CodeableConcept(text = str("Antenatal care contact"))),
      subject = subject,
      period =
        Period(
          start = FhirDateTimeElement(value = toFhirDateTime(visitDate)),
          end = FhirDateTimeElement(value = toFhirDateTime(visitDate)),
        ),
    )

  answers.decimal(LinkIds.WEIGHT)?.let { weight ->
    resources +=
      observation(
        code = codeableConcept(coding(Codes.LOINC, Codes.BODY_WEIGHT, "Body weight"), "Body weight"),
        value = Observation.Value.Quantity(quantity(weight, "kg", "kg")),
        category = VITAL_SIGNS,
      )
  }

  val systolic = answers.integer(LinkIds.SYSTOLIC)
  val diastolic = answers.integer(LinkIds.DIASTOLIC)
  if (systolic != null || diastolic != null) {
    resources +=
      Observation(
        id = "anc-obs-${UUID.randomUUID()}",
        status = Enumeration(value = Observation.ObservationStatus.Final),
        category = listOf(codeableConcept(VITAL_SIGNS)),
        code =
          codeableConcept(
            coding(Codes.LOINC, Codes.BLOOD_PRESSURE_PANEL, "Blood pressure panel with all children optional"),
            "Blood pressure",
          ),
        subject = subject,
        encounter = encounterRef,
        effective = effective,
        component =
          listOfNotNull(
            systolic?.let { bloodPressureComponent(Codes.SYSTOLIC, "Systolic blood pressure", it) },
            diastolic?.let { bloodPressureComponent(Codes.DIASTOLIC, "Diastolic blood pressure", it) },
          ),
      )
  }

  answers.integer(LinkIds.GESTATIONAL_AGE)?.let { weeks ->
    resources +=
      observation(
        code =
          codeableConcept(
            coding(Codes.LOINC, Codes.GESTATIONAL_AGE, "Gestational age Estimated"),
            "Gestational age",
          ),
        value = Observation.Value.Quantity(quantity(BigDecimal.fromInt(weeks), "weeks", "wk")),
      )
  }

  answers.codings(LinkIds.DANGER_SIGNS).forEach { sign ->
    resources +=
      observation(
        code = codeableConcept(coding(Codes.DANGER_SIGNS, DANGER_SIGN_CODE, "Danger sign"), "Danger sign"),
        value = Observation.Value.CodeableConcept(codeableConcept(sign, sign.display?.value)),
      )
  }

  answers.text(LinkIds.NOTES)?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }?.let { notes ->
    resources +=
      observation(
        code = codeableConcept(coding(Codes.LOINC, Codes.ANNOTATION_COMMENT, "Annotation comment"), "Notes"),
        value = Observation.Value.String(str(notes)),
      )
  }

  resources +=
    response.copy(
      id = "anc-qr-${UUID.randomUUID()}",
      questionnaire = Canonical(value = Codes.QUESTIONNAIRE_URL),
      status = Enumeration(value = QuestionnaireResponse.QuestionnaireResponseStatus.Completed),
      subject = subject,
      encounter = encounterRef,
      authored = FhirDateTimeElement(value = now()),
    )

  return resources
}

private const val DANGER_SIGN_CODE = "danger-sign"

private val VITAL_SIGNS = Coding(
  system = uri(Codes.OBSERVATION_CATEGORY),
  code = code("vital-signs"),
  display = str("Vital Signs"),
)

private fun bloodPressureComponent(loincCode: String, display: String, value: Int) =
  Observation.Component(
    code = codeableConcept(coding(Codes.LOINC, loincCode, display)),
    value = Observation.Component.Value.Quantity(quantity(BigDecimal.fromInt(value), "mmHg", "mm[Hg]")),
  )

private fun now(): FhirDateTime {
  val zone = TimeZone.currentSystemDefault()
  val instant = kotlin.time.Clock.System.now()
  return FhirDateTime.DateTime(instant.toLocalDateTime(zone), zone.offsetAt(instant))
}

/* ---------- reading the questionnaire response ---------- */

/** All answers in the response, flattened, keyed by link id. Groups nest their answers. */
private fun QuestionnaireResponse.answersByLinkId(): Map<String, List<QuestionnaireResponse.Answer>> {
  val result = mutableMapOf<String, MutableList<QuestionnaireResponse.Answer>>()
  fun visit(items: List<QuestionnaireResponse.Item>) {
    items.forEach { item ->
      result.getOrPut(item.linkId.value.orEmpty()) { mutableListOf() } += item.answer
      visit(item.item)
      item.answer.forEach { visit(it.item) }
    }
  }
  visit(item)
  return result
}

private fun Map<String, List<QuestionnaireResponse.Answer>>.first(linkId: String) =
  this[linkId]?.firstOrNull()?.value

private fun Map<String, List<QuestionnaireResponse.Answer>>.date(linkId: String): LocalDate? =
  (first(linkId) as? QuestionnaireResponse.Answer.Value.Date)?.value?.value.toLocalDate()

private fun Map<String, List<QuestionnaireResponse.Answer>>.integer(linkId: String): Int? =
  (first(linkId) as? QuestionnaireResponse.Answer.Value.Integer)?.value?.value

private fun Map<String, List<QuestionnaireResponse.Answer>>.decimal(linkId: String): BigDecimal? =
  (first(linkId) as? QuestionnaireResponse.Answer.Value.Decimal)?.value?.value

private fun Map<String, List<QuestionnaireResponse.Answer>>.text(linkId: String): String? =
  (first(linkId) as? QuestionnaireResponse.Answer.Value.String)?.value?.value

private fun Map<String, List<QuestionnaireResponse.Answer>>.codings(linkId: String): List<Coding> =
  this[linkId].orEmpty().mapNotNull { (it.value as? QuestionnaireResponse.Answer.Value.Coding)?.value }
KTEOF

  override fun getFhirEngine(): FhirEngine = FhirEngineProvider.getInstance(context)

  override fun getDownloadWorkManager() =
    ResourceParamsBasedDownloadWorkManager(
      linkedMapOf(
        ResourceType.Patient to emptyMap(),
        ResourceType.Encounter to emptyMap(),
        ResourceType.Observation to emptyMap(),
        ResourceType.Questionnaire to mapOf("_id" to Codes.QUESTIONNAIRE_ID),
      ),
      FullDownloadContext,
    )

  override fun getConflictResolver() = AcceptRemoteConflictResolver

  /**
   * New visits are created with ids assigned on the device, so they are uploaded with PUT to keep
   * the same id on the server.
   */
  override fun getUploadStrategy(): UploadStrategy =
    UploadStrategy.forIndividualRequest(
      methodForCreate = HttpCreateMethod.PUT,
      methodForUpdate = HttpUpdateMethod.PATCH,
      squash = true,
    )

  /**
   * A clinic register is small enough to pull in full every time, which keeps the device in step
   * with the server even when records are edited there.
   */
  private object FullDownloadContext : ResourceParamsBasedDownloadWorkManager.TimestampContext {
    override suspend fun saveLastUpdatedTimestamp(resourceType: ResourceType, timestamp: String?) = Unit

    override suspend fun getLasUpdateTimestamp(resourceType: ResourceType): String? = null
  }
}

/** Runs one full sync and reports how it finished. */
suspend fun syncWithServer(context: Context): SyncJobStatus =
  AncSyncTask(context).runSync(taskName = null, onProgress = {})

  curl -s -X DELETE "$B/Encounter/$id" -o /dev/null -w "Enc $id -> %{http_code}\n"
done
echo "--- remaining ---"
for t in Patient Encounter Observation QuestionnaireResponse Questionnaire; do echo -n "$t: "; curl -s "$B/$t?_summary=count" | python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('total'))"; done

aiTitle: Android ANC visit tracker for clinic

content.text:
The app is built, installed on the emulator, and verified end to end against the live HAPI server.

## What's there

**Data layer** (`data/`)
- `AncSync.kt` — a `FhirSyncTask` that pulls `Patient`, `Encounter`, `Observation` and the `anc-contact` `Questionnaire` into the FHIR Engine's local database and pushes locally recorded resources back up. Runs on the app's own coroutine scope via `runSync`, so no WorkManager plumbing. New resources get device-assigned ids and upload with PUT so they keep those ids on the server.
- `AncRepository.kt` — reads the register from the local engine (Patients that have a `11778-8` estimated-due-date observation still in the future, sorted soonest-first), assembles visits by grouping a patient's observations under their encounters, and serialises the Questionnaire to the JSON string the Data Capture library takes.
- `VisitExtraction.kt` — turns a completed `QuestionnaireResponse` into an `Encounter`, an `Observation` per measurement (weight `29463-7`, BP panel `85354-9` with systolic/diastolic components, gestational age `11884-4`, one per danger sign, notes `48767-8`), plus the response itself for provenance.
- `Models.kt` — age from date of birth, and weeks of pregnancy derived from the due date on a 280-day term.

**UI** (`ui/`) — Compose Material 3: register list → patient detail (visits newest first, with a "Record visit" FAB) → the Data Capture `Questionnaire` composable rendering the server's form. The form is scoped to its own `ViewModelStore` so each visit starts blank rather than reusing the previous answers.

## Verified on the emulator
- Register shows Grace (32 wks, due 15 Oct), Emily (25 wks, due 5 Dec), Sarah (19 wks, due 20 Jan) in due-date order with correct ages.
- Detail screen shows each patient's seeded visit with weight, BP and hemoglobin.
- Recorded a new visit for Grace (26 Aug 2026, 33 wks, 73.4 kg, 120/78, severe headache + blurred vision, notes) — it appeared in her visit list, survived a force-stop and relaunch, and landed on the server as an `Encounter`, six `Observation`s and a `QuestionnaireResponse`.
- Required-field validation blocks an empty visit date; I turned off the library's "Submit anyway" escape hatch since a visit with no date can't be filed.

## Two things to flag
- I bumped `sourceCompatibility`/`jvmTarget` from 17 to 21 — `fhir-engine`'s inline functions are compiled against JVM 21 and won't inline into 17 bytecode. I also added `lifecycle-viewmodel-compose`/`lifecycle-runtime-compose` 2.9.4 (2.11.0 needs AGP 9.1) and `kotlinx-serialization-json`, since the FHIR AARs expose those only as runtime deps.
- After testing I deleted the visit I created from the HAPI server and cleared app data, so the server is back to the three patients with one prior visit each.
